analysis:
Reviewed the two CHANGELOG.md head_text units (lines 5476-5947) and the patch excerpt, which shows only documentation: a new v0.10.13 candidate heading with highlights and rollout notes. No executable code, configuration, workflow, or security control is changed in the supplied evidence.

The visible text is historical release-note content about App Attest key rotation limits, enrollment backoff, APNs code-identity retries, diagnostics, and earlier releases. It states that diagnostics are outside the signed transcript, do not affect authorization, and are bounded. Rotation never revokes or denies serving. Other entries describe fail-closed serving authorization and release qualification. These statements are consistent with TB-011 and T-052 to T-058. They are claims in a changelog, not verified implementation, so I did not treat them as proof of the controls.

The unit-56 changelog sections describe diagnostics reporting (launch_session, boot_time, native error chains, device-wide devicecheckd matches) and `darkbloom report` reading user credentials under sudo. That is existing behavior documented in prose. Without the source I cannot verify it. It touches T-058 (diagnostic leakage) and A-008 (token custody), and those code paths would need review in a PR that actually changes them. The cache-related entries (SSD prefix cache, TTL, scoping) match T-041's accepted posture. No new TTL or scope loosening is introduced here.

The patch excerpt is truncated, so the tail of the new v0.10.13 section was not visible. The visible portion mentions a Gemma loop-exit guard (default-on, env opt-out, Gemma 4 only, never with logprobs) and pair-setup stop handling; those code changes live in other files that were not supplied. Integration should examine those files for the loop-exit behavior affecting output integrity (T-007 is provider-side and adversarial anyway) and for the stop-request handling in pair setup (availability, A-018). No findings are raised from this docs-only change.
